cohort: 1,515,263 women from the National Vital Statistics System (NVSS) 2020
finding: An interpregnancy interval (IPI) of 18-23 months was associated with a lower risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) compared to an IPI of 24-59 months.
mod_finding: The study found that the association between interpregnancy interval and gestational diabetes mellitus varied among groups with different histories of cesarean section.
